notes: Extracted 29 October 2026 from the guide and its evidence at b4988c5. The guide's Sources note was checked on 23 October 2026 on the 23 October build (mirror v0.1.78-c8526ae, the #281 fix that made the dialog role and focus trap opt-in through trapFocus); the evidence's Contract was checked on 12 October on v0.1.78-636f3f5, its accessibility re-checked on a116616 (17 October) and c8526ae (23 October), and the c8526ae section replaces the older ones where they differ. Installed build: jfs-components 0.1.78, mirror v0.1.78-dbe0e02 (Biscuit's main at dbe0e02, 27 October); its Overlay.tsx and web focus trap still match the c8526ae contract (the placement styles, fill, the inert scrim without onPress, trapFocus as the only way to the dialog role, Tab and Escape handled by the newest trap only), read from source, not run. The guide names no other component to use instead, so the avoidWhen rule (stacked scrims) has no useInstead; ModalSheet is not named. The examples are the guide's own confirmation dialog (a Card holding a Title and a ButtonGroup with Pay and Cancel, the Card's 16 px margin and the Title's two lines kept) with the guide's modes except Color Mode Light: the Card's AppearanceBrand Neutral (white, the evidence's fix of the cream default after Marcin's 12 October review), the Buttons' AppearanceBrand Primary (a Card passes its modes to its children) and Cancel's Emphasis Low (the evidence: the low-emphasis way out Figma's Popup uses for Later). The first extraction dropped these for the building rules' slot defaults and Emphasis Medium; the cross-check flagged that as unsupported, and the guide decides this dialog, so the examples follow it. The docked example keeps trapFocus and the name because its content is still a dialog (the guide's Content names trapFocus for a dialog; its configuration previews leave trapFocus off because, as its Sources note says, only the In context dialog on that page uses it); the bare-scrim example leaves it off, as the package says for a scrim drawn under another surface. Not recorded as gaps: the scrim's colour being the same in every Color Mode (dark mode belongs to the brand team), and #269 and #281, both fixed (the evidence's Coin gaps list still shows #269 as To do, but its Checked and Contract sections say the re-test passed).

examples.purpose: Confirming a payment, the guide's In context dialog: the overlay dims the screen and holds a dialog that keeps keyboard focus (trapFocus), named “Cancel payment”. As in the guide, the Card is white (AppearanceBrand Neutral), its buttons set AppearanceBrand Primary because a Card passes its modes to its children, and Cancel is the low-emphasis way out (Emphasis Low). Pay completes it; Cancel, Escape or a tap on the scrim backs out, and the screen removes the overlay either way.
examples.jsx:
<Overlay
  trapFocus
  dismissAccessibilityLabel="Cancel payment"
  onPress={() => {}}
>
  <Card modes={{ AppearanceBrand: 'Neutral' }} style={{ margin: 16 }}>
    <Title title="Confirm payment" subtitle="₹250 to Ravi Stores" numberOfLines={2} />
    <ButtonGroup>
      <Button label="Pay" onPress={() => {}} modes={{ AppearanceBrand: 'Primary' }} />
      <Button label="Cancel" onPress={() => {}} modes={{ AppearanceBrand: 'Primary', Emphasis: 'Low' }} />
    </ButtonGroup>
  </Card>
</Overlay>

from.quote: Pay ₹250 dims Home and asks for confirmation in a dialog that holds keyboard focus (trapFocus).

evidenceFacts.name: contentPlacement
evidenceFacts.description: center: content centred at its own width; top and bottom: docked to that edge and stretched across; stretch: centred vertically and stretched across.

evidenceFacts.name: onPress
evidenceFacts.description: With onPress, a full-size scrim under the content calls it, so presses on the content don't dismiss; without it the scrim is inert but still blocks presses to the page.
evidenceFacts.quote: No `onPress`: the scrim is inert but still blocks presses to the page.

evidenceFacts.name: fill
evidenceFacts.description: true: an absolute fill of the nearest positioned parent (on the web every React Native View is positioned), not the viewport. false: in the page's flow, sized by its content or style.
evidenceFacts.quote: absolute fill of the nearest positioned parent (every React Native View is positioned on the web), not the viewport.

evidenceFacts.name: trapFocus
evidenceFacts.description: Only with trapFocus is the overlay a dialog: role dialog and aria-modal on the web (accessibilityViewIsModal on native), named accessibilityLabel ?? dismissAccessibilityLabel. On the web focus moves inside on mount, Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside, Escape calls onPress, and focus returns to the opener when it's removed; only the newest mounted trapFocus overlay handles Tab and Escape. Without it the overlay doesn't move focus, trap Tab or take a dialog role.
evidenceFacts.quote: focus returns to the opener when it's removed

evidenceFacts.name: dismissAccessibilityLabel
evidenceFacts.description: Names the dialog when trapFocus is set (accessibilityLabel wins when it is set). Without trapFocus it stays the label of the scrim with onPress, which is hidden from screen readers and is not a Tab stop.

evidenceFacts.name: modes
evidenceFacts.description: Cascade to the children, merged under their own modes. The scrim reads one token, overlay/background (rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.7)), the same in every mode.
evidenceFacts.quote: Children get the overlay's `modes` merged under their own (`cloneChildrenWithModes`).
